evals.prompt: Review this Containerfile fragment: FROM scratch; COPY app /app; USER 65532; HEALTHCHECK CMD curl http://localhost:8080/health; ENTRYPOINT ["/app"]. The binary is static but curl is not copied.
evals.expected_output: Identify that the health command/shell cannot run in scratch, propose an app subcommand or runtime probe, and distinguish OCI metadata support.

evals.prompt: Review a compose service with ENTRYPOINT ["/app"] in its image and command: ["migrate"]. The image implements migrate and runs non-root with a writable volume.
evals.expected_output: Accept the entrypoint/CMD combination; do not add /app again or demand an unrelated architecture.

evals.prompt: Can I copy a venv from python:3.12-slim-bookworm to distroless/python3-debian12 and assume it runs? Also check these choices against our runtime policy.
evals.expected_output: Allow the Python build-only image, identify the final distroless runtime as outside the list, and explain interpreter path/version, ABI and library closure checks. Propose an allowed final runtime without requiring an allowlisted builder.

evals.prompt: Our project uses Docker BuildKit. Fix RUN --mount=type=bind,source=go.mod,target=go.mod,z go mod download failing on the z option. Keep Docker.
evals.expected_output: Remove the unsupported option or use portable COPY, preserve Docker, and avoid claiming Docker ignores Buildah-specific flags.

evals.prompt: Review a pinned golang builder producing a CGO_ENABLED=0 executable copied into a final FROM scratch stage. Is the builder a policy violation?
evals.expected_output: Do not flag the build-only golang image. Apply the allowlist to the scratch deliverable, then verify actual static linkage and needed runtime files without claiming an unrun smoke test passed.

evals.prompt: A Containerfile uses quay.io/buildah/stable as a donor, collects its verified executable, libraries and configuration, then copies that closure into scratch. Must we replace the donor just because it is absent from the allowlist?
evals.expected_output: No. Donor images are not restricted by the final-runtime list. Check closure, compatibility, licenses and actual execution; do not demand a rebuild solely because of the donor repository.

evals.prompt: The default final stage is scratch, but this release publishes --target build, whose FROM is golang. Which target should the runtime allowlist inspect?
evals.expected_output: Inspect the explicitly delivered build target and its inherited runtime base. The unused scratch stage does not establish compliance, and internal build-cache stages must not be confused with published targets.
